CHAPTER 30 — मुद्रणत्रुटिशोधनम् (MUDRANA-TRUTI-SHODHANAM — CORRECTING PRINTING ERRORS)

Introduction — मुद्रणत्रुटिः किम्?

The word मुद्रणत्रुटिशोधनम् is made of three parts: मुद्रणम् (printing), त्रुटिः (an error, a slip) and शोधनम् (correction, purification). Together it means 'the correction of printing errors' — in English, proof-reading. When a Sanskrit text is typed or printed, small mistakes creep in: a wrong letter, a missing vowel-sign (मात्रा), a dropped anusvāra (ं) or visarga (ः), a badly joined सन्धि, a wrong case-ending (विभक्ति), a broken conjunct (संयुक्ताक्षर), or words wrongly split or joined. In Sanskrit even a tiny slip can change the meaning completely — मासः means 'a month' but मांसः means 'flesh'; दिनम् means 'a day' but दीनम् means 'a poor, wretched thing'. The person who reads a printed proof and marks such errors is the संशोधकः (proof-reader), and his careful work is called संशोधनम् or शोधनम्. This lesson is a practical, editorial-skills lesson: it teaches you to spot each kind of error, to know the grammatical rule that fixes it, and to proof-read whole passages methodically.

Why this skill matters (शोधनस्य महत्त्वम्)

Sanskrit is a precision language. Its grammar packs meaning into single sounds: the visarga of रामः marks the subject; the anusvāra of रामं marks the object; the halant of भगवान् marks a consonant-ending word. A printer who drops one dot has changed the grammar of the sentence. For an editor, teacher, typist or student of Sanskrit, त्रुटिशोधनम् is therefore not mere cosmetic polishing — it is the guarding of meaning (अर्थरक्षणम्). A good proof-reader needs two things: (1) a sharp, patient eye (सूक्ष्मदृष्टिः), and (2) sound grammar (व्याकरणज्ञानम्) — because you can only correct an error if you know what the correct form must be.

THE SEVEN COMMON ERROR TYPES (सप्त प्रमुखत्रुटयः)

(1) अक्षरत्रुटिः — wrong letter. One consonant is printed in place of another. The commonest confusions are ब/व, ण/न and श/ष/स.
  • रामायनम् → रामायणम् : by the णत्व rule, न becomes ण after र् within the same word; hence रामायणम्, कारणम् (not कारनम्), प्रणामः (not प्रनामः), परिणामः (not परिनामः).
  • भासा → भाषा ; पुरुशः → पुरुषः ; दोशः → दोषः : by the षत्व rule, the स of certain suffixes becomes ष after vowels other than अ/आ and after र्; hence भाषा, पुरुषः, दोषः, विशेषः.
  • वालकः → बालकः ; बनम् → वनम् : ब and व are different letters — बालकः (boy) begins with ब, वनम् (forest) begins with व.

(2) मात्रात्रुटिः — wrong vowel-sign. A short vowel-sign is printed for a long one, or vice versa (इ/ई, उ/ऊ).
  • परिक्षा → परीक्षा (परि + ईक्षा gives the long ई) ; सुर्यः → सूर्यः ; किर्तिः → कीर्तिः ; नदि → नदी ; पुजा → पूजा ; मुर्खः → मूर्खः ; भुमिः → भूमिः ; जिवनम् → जीवनम् ; दिपः → दीपः ; शिघ्रम् → शीघ्रम्.
  • The opposite error also occurs: गुरूः → गुरुः (the stem गुरु has short उ) ; मधूरम् → मधुरम्.
  • Some matra errors change the meaning entirely: दिनम् (day) / दीनम् (wretched) ; सुतः (son) / सूतः (charioteer). Such meaning-changing errors are the most dangerous of all.

(3) सन्धित्रुटिः — wrong or omitted sandhi. When two words are joined, the sounds at the junction must change by rule. Printing the words merely glued together, or joined by a wrong rule, is a sandhi error.
  • दीर्घसन्धिः (अ/आ + अ/आ = आ ; इ/ई + इ/ई = ई ; उ/ऊ + उ/ऊ = ऊ): विद्याआलयः → विद्यालयः ; हिमआलयः → हिमालयः.
  • गुणसन्धिः (अ/आ + इ/ई = ए ; अ/आ + उ/ऊ = ओ ; अ/आ + ऋ = अर्): देवइन्द्रः → देवेन्द्रः ; गणईशः → गणेशः ; सूर्यउदयः → सूर्योदयः ; महाऋषिः → महर्षिः.
  • वृद्धिसन्धिः (अ/आ + ए/ऐ = ऐ ; अ/आ + ओ/औ = औ): सदाएव → सदैव ; एकएकम् → एकैकम् ; महाऔषधम् → महौषधम्.
  • यण्सन्धिः (इ/ई → य्, उ/ऊ → व् before an unlike vowel): इतिआदि → इत्यादि ; सुआगतम् → स्वागतम् ; प्रतिएकम् → प्रत्येकम्.
  • व्यञ्जनसन्धिः (consonant junctions): सत्जनः → सज्जनः (त् + ज् = ज्ज्) ; उत्चारणम् → उच्चारणम् (त् + च् = च्च्) ; जगत्नाथः → जगन्नाथः (त् + न् = न्न्) ; तत्लीनः → तल्लीनः (त् + ल् = ल्ल्).

(4) विभक्तित्रुटिः — wrong case-ending, or wrong agreement of the verb or adjective. To correct these you must remember the roles of the seven cases.
  • The subject stands in प्रथमा: रामं वनं गच्छति → रामः वनं गच्छति.
  • The object and the destination stand in द्वितीया: सः विद्यालयः गच्छति → सः विद्यालयं गच्छति ; बालकः दुग्धः पिबति → बालकः दुग्धं पिबति.
  • The instrument stands in तृतीया: छात्रः लेखनी लिखति → छात्रः लेखन्या लिखति (writes WITH a pen).
  • The receiver stands in चतुर्थी: सः निर्धनाय वस्त्रं ददाति (gives TO the poor man).
  • The point of separation stands in पञ्चमी: बालकः वृक्षस्य पतति → बालकः वृक्षात् पतति (falls FROM the tree).
  • Possession is षष्ठी: रामस्य पुस्तकम् (Rama's book) ; place/time is सप्तमी: सः नगरे वसति (lives IN the city) ; address is सम्बोधनम्: हे बालक! (not हे बालकः!).
  • Agreement errors belong here too: बालकाः पठति → बालकाः पठन्ति (plural subject needs a plural verb) ; अहं पठति → अहं पठामि ; त्वं गच्छति → त्वं गच्छसि ; वयं गच्छति → वयं गच्छामः ; and gender agreement: सुन्दरः बालिका → सुन्दरी बालिका ; श्वेतः वस्त्रम् → श्वेतं वस्त्रम्.

(5) अनुस्वारत्रुटिः — missing or misplaced anusvāra (ं) or nasal consonant.
  • सस्कृतम् → संस्कृतम् ; ससारः → संसारः ; सुदरम् → सुन्दरम् ; गगा → गङ्गा ; वदे → वन्दे.
  • An added anusvāra can also change meaning: मासः (month) is not मांसः (flesh). Check every dot!

(6) विसर्गत्रुटिः — missing or misplaced visarga (ः).
  • दुखम् → दुःखम् ; अन्तकरणम् → अन्तःकरणम् ; पुन → पुनः ; प्रातकालः → प्रातःकालः ; अत → अतः ; नम → नमः.
  • Sentence-subjects often lose their visarga in print: बालक क्रीडति → बालकः क्रीडति.
  • Visarga-sandhi must also be checked: मनःरथः → मनोरथः ; निःचयः → निश्चयः ; नमःते → नमस्ते ; पुनःअपि → पुनरपि.

(7) संयुक्ताक्षर-हलन्त-पदच्छेदत्रुटयः — broken conjuncts, missing halants, and wrong word-division.
  • Conjunct errors: विदया → विद्या ; उतमः → उत्तमः ; प्रशनः → प्रश्नः ; वाकयम् → वाक्यम् ; अधययनम् → अध्ययनम् ; विदवान् → विद्वान् ; धरमः → धर्मः ; करम → कर्म ; सरवे → सर्वे.
  • Halant errors: भगवान → भगवान् ; जगत → जगत् ; हनुमान → हनुमान् ; भवान → भवान् (consonant-ending words need the हलन्त stroke).
  • Word-division (पदच्छेद) errors: सःपाठंपठति → सः पाठं पठति (words wrongly glued together) ; विद्या लयः → विद्यालयः (one word wrongly split in two).

व्याकरण-स्मरणम् — GRAMMAR REFRESHER FOR THE PROOF-READER

(A) सन्धि rules in brief. दीर्घ: like simple vowels merge into the long vowel (अ+अ=आ, इ+इ=ई, उ+उ=ऊ). गुण: अ/आ + इ/ई = ए ; + उ/ऊ = ओ ; + ऋ = अर्. वृद्धि: अ/आ + ए/ऐ = ऐ ; + ओ/औ = औ. यण्: इ/ई, उ/ऊ, ऋ become य्, व्, र् before an unlike vowel. विसर्गसन्धिः: the visarga becomes ओ before soft (voiced) sounds (मनः + रथः = मनोरथः), becomes श्/ष्/स् before the matching hard sounds (निश्चयः, नमस्ते), and becomes र् in forms like पुनरपि. Whenever you suspect a sandhi error, SPLIT the form (सन्धिविच्छेदः), apply the rule afresh, and re-join.

(B) विभक्ति endings of the a-stem राम, singular: प्रथमा रामः, द्वितीया रामम्, तृतीया रामेण, चतुर्थी रामाय, पञ्चमी रामात्, षष्ठी रामस्य, सप्तमी रामे, सम्बोधन हे राम. Their roles: subject; object/destination; instrument (by/with); recipient (to/for); source (from); possession (of); location (in/at); address. A proof-reader silently asks of every noun: what is this word DOING in the sentence, and does its ending match that role?

(C) अनुस्वार-विसर्ग rules. A word-final म् before a consonant is written as the anusvāra dot (अहं गच्छामि); before a vowel it stays म् and usually joins (धनम् + आप्नोति = धनमाप्नोति). The visarga ः is a real sound — dropping it turns दुःखम् into the meaningless दुखम् and strips the subject-marker from बालकः. Nasal conjuncts (न्द, ङ्ग, ण्ड) must not be flattened: सुन्दरम्, गङ्गा, दण्डः.

शोधनविधिः — THE METHOD OF CAREFUL PROOF-READING

1. मूलपाठेन तुलना — keep the original manuscript beside the proof and compare line by line; never trust memory.
2. शब्दशः पठनम् — read word by word, not by the flow of sense. The eye that reads for meaning silently 'auto-corrects' errors and slides past them; the proof-reader must read what is actually printed, not what ought to be printed.
3. मात्रा-बिन्दु-परीक्षा — check every vowel-sign, every anusvāra dot, every visarga and every halant stroke, letter by letter, especially in unfamiliar words.
4. व्याकरणपरीक्षा — test every junction by the sandhi rules and every noun-ending by the vibhakti roles; split doubtful sandhis and re-join them by rule.
5. उच्चैः पठनम् — read the text aloud once; the ear catches wrong vowels and broken rhythm that the eye misses.
6. द्वितीयं पठनम् — always give the proof a second pass, ideally after a gap, or hand it to a second reader; fresh eyes find what tired eyes forgive.
7. संशोधनचिह्नानि — mark each correction clearly in the margin with standard proof-marks; never scribble over the text itself.

अभ्यासः — PRACTICE PASSAGES (find and fix)

Passage 1 (with errors): रामः प्रतिदिनं विधालयं गच्छति। सः सस्कृतं पठति। तस्य परिक्षा शीघ्रं भविष्यति। सः उतमः छात्रः अस्ति।
Corrected: रामः प्रतिदिनं विद्यालयं गच्छति। सः संस्कृतं पठति। तस्य परीक्षा शीघ्रं भविष्यति। सः उत्तमः छात्रः अस्ति।
(Fixes: विधालयं → विद्यालयं, broken conjunct द्य ; सस्कृतं → संस्कृतं, missing anusvāra ; परिक्षा → परीक्षा, long ई matra ; उतमः → उत्तमः, double त्त.)

Passage 2 (with errors): सूर्यउदयः अतीव सुदरः भवति। बालकाः नदि-तीरे क्रीडति। ते दुखम् न जानन्ति।
Corrected: सूर्योदयः अतीव सुन्दरः भवति। बालकाः नदी-तीरे क्रीडन्ति। ते दुःखं न जानन्ति।
(Fixes: सूर्यउदयः → सूर्योदयः, guna sandhi अ+उ=ओ ; सुदरः → सुन्दरः, nasal न् ; नदि → नदी, long ई ; क्रीडति → क्रीडन्ति, plural verb ; दुखम् → दुःखं, missing visarga and म् → ं before a consonant.)

SUMMARY (सारांश)

मुद्रणत्रुटिशोधनम् is the editorial skill of finding and correcting printing errors in Sanskrit text. The seven common error families are: अक्षरत्रुटिः (wrong letter — watch ब/व, ण/न, श/ष/स and the णत्व/षत्व rules), मात्रात्रुटिः (short/long vowel-sign — परीक्षा, सूर्यः, नदी), सन्धित्रुटिः (apply the दीर्घ, गुण, वृद्धि, यण्, व्यञ्जन and विसर्ग rules — सूर्योदयः, इत्यादि, सज्जनः, मनोरथः), विभक्तित्रुटिः (case-roles and agreement — सः विद्यालयं गच्छति, बालकाः पठन्ति), अनुस्वारत्रुटिः (संस्कृतम्, गङ्गा — and the meaning-changing मासः/मांसः), विसर्गत्रुटिः (दुःखम्, पुनः, नमस्ते), and संयुक्ताक्षर/हलन्त/पदच्छेद errors (विद्या, प्रश्नः, भगवान्, सः पाठं पठति). The method is sevenfold: compare with the original, read word by word, inspect every matra and dot, test junctions and endings by grammar, read aloud, give a second pass, and mark corrections cleanly in the margin. Careful proof-reading is अर्थरक्षणम् — the guarding of meaning itself.

topics.name: मुद्रणत्रुटिः — Nature and Importance of Printing Errors
topics.description: What मुद्रणत्रुटिशोधनम् (proof-reading) means — मुद्रणम् + त्रुटिः + शोधनम्; why even tiny slips (a dot, a matra) can change meaning in Sanskrit (मासः/मांसः, दिनम्/दीनम्); and the proof-reader's two tools: a patient eye (सूक्ष्मदृष्टिः) and sound grammar (व्याकरणज्ञानम्).

topics.name: त्रुटिवर्गीकरणम् — The Seven Error Types
topics.description: The taxonomy of common printing errors: अक्षरत्रुटिः (wrong letter), मात्रात्रुटिः (wrong vowel-sign), सन्धित्रुटिः, विभक्तित्रुटिः, अनुस्वारत्रुटिः, विसर्गत्रुटिः, and संयुक्ताक्षर/हलन्त/पदच्छेद errors — with a marker example of each type.

topics.name: अक्षर-मात्रा-त्रुटयः — Letter and Vowel-sign Errors
topics.description: Correcting wrong-letter errors (ब/व confusion; ण/न via the णत्व rule — रामायणम्, कारणम्; श/ष/स via the षत्व rule — भाषा, पुरुषः) and wrong vowel-sign errors (इ/ई, उ/ऊ — परीक्षा, सूर्यः, नदी, गुरुः), including meaning-changing matra errors like दिनम्/दीनम्.

topics.name: सन्धित्रुटयः — Sandhi Errors and their Correction
topics.description: Detecting and fixing wrongly joined words using the sandhi rules: दीर्घ (विद्यालयः), गुण (सूर्योदयः, देवेन्द्रः), वृद्धि (सदैव), यण् (इत्यादि, स्वागतम्), व्यञ्जन (सज्जनः, जगन्नाथः) and विसर्ग sandhi (मनोरथः, निश्चयः, नमस्ते) — by सन्धिविच्छेद and re-joining by rule.

topics.name: विभक्ति-अनुस्वार-विसर्ग-त्रुटयः — Case, Anusvara and Visarga Errors
topics.description: Correcting wrong case-endings by the roles of the seven vibhaktis (subject प्रथमा, object/destination द्वितीया, instrument तृतीया, recipient चतुर्थी, source पञ्चमी, possession षष्ठी, location सप्तमी), verb and gender agreement (बालकाः पठन्ति, सुन्दरी बालिका), missing anusvāras (संस्कृतम्, गङ्गा) and visargas (दुःखम्, पुनः, बालकः).

topics.name: शोधनविधिः — Method of Proof-reading and Practice
topics.description: The seven-step proof-reading method — comparison with the original, word-by-word reading, matra-and-dot inspection, grammar checks, reading aloud, a second pass, and clean margin marks — plus conjunct/halant/word-division fixes and practice passages with errors to find and correct.

chapter_summary.title: मुद्रणत्रुटिशोधनम् (Mudrana-Truti-Shodhanam) — Chapter Summary
chapter_summary.intro: This is the NIOS Senior Secondary Sanskrit (309) summary for Chapter 30. It teaches the practical editorial skill of proof-reading Sanskrit: the seven common families of printing errors, the grammar rules (सन्धि, विभक्ति, अनुस्वार-विसर्ग) that fix them, and a seven-step method for reading proofs carefully.

sections.heading: What proof-reading is and why it matters
bullets: मुद्रणत्रुटिशोधनम् = मुद्रणम् (printing) + त्रुटिः (error) + शोधनम् (correction): the careful correction of printing errors, done by a संशोधकः (proof-reader).
Sanskrit packs grammar into single sounds — the visarga of रामः marks the subject, the anusvāra of रामं marks the object — so one dropped dot changes the grammar of a sentence.
Some errors change meaning entirely: मासः (month) vs मांसः (flesh), दिनम् (day) vs दीनम् (wretched); proof-reading is therefore अर्थरक्षणम्, the guarding of meaning.
The proof-reader needs a patient eye (सूक्ष्मदृष्टिः) and sound grammar (व्याकरणज्ञानम्) — you can only fix an error if you know what the correct form must be.

sections.heading: Letter and vowel-sign errors (अक्षर-मात्रा)
bullets: अक्षरत्रुटिः prints one consonant for another; the classic confusions are ब/व (बालकः not वालकः), ण/न and श/ष/स.
णत्व rule: न becomes ण after र् in the same word — रामायणम्, कारणम्, प्रणामः, परिणामः.
षत्व rule: स becomes ष after vowels other than अ/आ and after र् — भाषा, पुरुषः, दोषः, विशेषः.
मात्रात्रुटिः swaps short and long vowel-signs: परिक्षा → परीक्षा, सुर्यः → सूर्यः, नदि → नदी, गुरूः → गुरुः; meaning-changing pairs like दिनम्/दीनम् are the most dangerous.

sections.heading: Sandhi errors and their rules
bullets: दीर्घ: like vowels merge long — विद्या + आलयः = विद्यालयः, हिम + आलयः = हिमालयः.
गुण: अ/आ + इ/ई = ए, + उ/ऊ = ओ, + ऋ = अर् — देवेन्द्रः, गणेशः, सूर्योदयः, महर्षिः; वृद्धि: आ + ए = ऐ — सदैव, महौषधम्.
यण्: इ/उ become य्/व् before an unlike vowel — इत्यादि, स्वागतम्, प्रत्येकम्; व्यञ्जन: सत् + जनः = सज्जनः, जगत् + नाथः = जगन्नाथः, उत् + चारणम् = उच्चारणम्.
विसर्ग sandhi: मनः + रथः = मनोरथः, निः + चयः = निश्चयः, नमः + ते = नमस्ते, पुनः + अपि = पुनरपि.
Correction method: split the doubtful form (सन्धिविच्छेदः), apply the rule afresh, and re-join.

sections.heading: Case-ending, agreement, anusvara and visarga errors
bullets: Case roles: subject प्रथमा (रामः), object/destination द्वितीया (विद्यालयं गच्छति), instrument तृतीया (लेखन्या), recipient चतुर्थी (निर्धनाय), source पञ्चमी (वृक्षात् पतति), possession षष्ठी (रामस्य), location सप्तमी (नगरे), address हे राम.
Agreement: plural subject takes a plural verb (बालकाः पठन्ति), and person must match (अहं पठामि, त्वं गच्छसि, वयं गच्छामः); adjectives agree in gender (सुन्दरी बालिका, श्वेतं वस्त्रम्).
Anusvāra errors: सस्कृतम् → संस्कृतम्, ससारः → संसारः, गगा → गङ्गा, सुदरम् → सुन्दरम्; an added dot changes मासः to मांसः.
Visarga errors: दुखम् → दुःखम्, पुन → पुनः, अन्तकरणम् → अन्तःकरणम्, and dropped subject-markers like बालक क्रीडति → बालकः क्रीडति.
Conjunct and halant errors: विदया → विद्या, प्रशनः → प्रश्नः, उतमः → उत्तमः, भगवान → भगवान्, जगत → जगत्.

sections.heading: The seven-step proof-reading method
bullets: Compare the proof with the original line by line (मूलपाठेन तुलना) — never trust memory.
Read word by word (शब्दशः पठनम्): the eye reading for sense silently auto-corrects and slides past errors; read what is printed, not what ought to be.
Inspect every matra, anusvāra dot, visarga and halant stroke (मात्रा-बिन्दु-परीक्षा), and test every junction and ending by grammar (व्याकरणपरीक्षा).
Read aloud once (उच्चैः पठनम्) — the ear catches what the eye misses — and always give a second pass or a second reader (द्वितीयं पठनम्).
Mark corrections cleanly in the margin with standard proof-marks (संशोधनचिह्नानि), never over the text itself.

key_takeaways: मुद्रणत्रुटिशोधनम् is proof-reading: finding and correcting printing errors so that the meaning of the Sanskrit text is preserved (अर्थरक्षणम्).
The seven error families are अक्षर, मात्रा, सन्धि, विभक्ति, अनुस्वार, विसर्ग and संयुक्ताक्षर/हलन्त/पदच्छेद errors.
णत्व makes रामायणम् and कारणम् correct (never रामायनम्, कारनम्); षत्व makes भाषा and पुरुषः correct.
To fix a sandhi error, split the form and re-join by rule: सूर्य + उदयः = सूर्योदयः (गुण), इति + आदि = इत्यादि (यण्), मनः + रथः = मनोरथः (विसर्ग).
Every noun-ending must match the word's role: सः विद्यालयं गच्छति (destination द्वितीया), बालकः वृक्षात् पतति (source पञ्चमी); and बालकाः पठन्ति (plural agreement).
One dot matters: संस्कृतम् needs its anusvāra, दुःखम् its visarga — and मासः (month) must never become मांसः (flesh).
Proof-read methodically: compare with the original, read word by word and aloud, check every matra and dot, give a second pass, and mark corrections in the margin.

glossary.definition: A printing error — any slip of letter, matra, dot, sandhi, case-ending or word-division that enters a text during typing or printing.
Correction, purification; in this lesson, the systematic correcting of printing errors (proof-reading).
The proof-reader — the person who reads a printed proof, finds its errors and marks their corrections.
A wrong-letter error: one consonant printed for another, e.g. वालकः for बालकः, रामायनम् for रामायणम्.
A wrong vowel-sign error: a short matra printed for a long one or vice versa, e.g. परिक्षा for परीक्षा, नदि for नदी.
The rule by which न becomes ण after र् within a word — hence रामायणम्, कारणम्, प्रणामः, परिणामः.
The rule by which स becomes ष after vowels other than अ/आ and after र् — hence भाषा, पुरुषः, दोषः, विशेषः.
Splitting a joined (sandhi) form back into its separate words in order to check or re-apply the joining rule, e.g. सूर्योदयः = सूर्य + उदयः.
A noun's case-ending, showing its role: प्रथमा subject, द्वितीया object/destination, तृतीया instrument, चतुर्थी recipient, पञ्चमी source, षष्ठी possession, सप्तमी location.
The nasal dot ं, as in संस्कृतम्, रामं; its omission or wrong addition is an अनुस्वारत्रुटिः (मासः vs मांसः).
The sound written ः, as in रामः, दुःखम्, पुनः; a real sound whose omission strips grammar and meaning from the word.
A conjunct consonant cluster such as द्य in विद्या, श्न in प्रश्नः, त्त in उत्तमः; printing it flattened (विदया, प्रशनः, उतमः) is a conjunct error.
The stroke that marks a bare consonant at a word's end, as in भगवान्, जगत्, विद्वान्; omitting it is a halant error.
Word-division; wrongly gluing words together (सःपाठंपठति) or splitting one word in two (विद्या लयः) is a पदच्छेद error.
Standard proof-marks written in the margin of a proof to show each correction clearly, without scribbling over the text.

worksheet.title: Worksheet — मुद्रणत्रुटिशोधनम् (NIOS Sanskrit 309, Chapter 30)
worksheet.instructions: Attempt all questions. Write Sanskrit words in Devanagari and give your explanations in English. For every correction, name the error type and state the rule on which the correction rests.

questions.question: What is मुद्रणत्रुटिशोधनम्? Break the word into its three parts and explain why this skill is called अर्थरक्षणम् (the guarding of meaning).
questions.answer: मुद्रणत्रुटिशोधनम् = मुद्रणम् (printing) + त्रुटिः (error) + शोधनम् (correction): the correction of printing errors, i.e. proof-reading. It is called अर्थरक्षणम् because in Sanskrit a single slip can change the meaning — मासः (month) becomes मांसः (flesh), दिनम् (day) becomes दीनम् (wretched) — so correcting errors literally guards the meaning of the text.
questions.explanation: Definition by word-parts plus the meaning-change argument.

questions.question: Name any five of the seven error families taught in this lesson, and give one wrong → correct example for each.
questions.answer: 1) अक्षरत्रुटिः (wrong letter): रामायनम् → रामायणम्. 2) मात्रात्रुटिः (wrong vowel-sign): परिक्षा → परीक्षा. 3) सन्धित्रुटिः: सूर्यउदयः → सूर्योदयः. 4) विभक्तित्रुटिः: सः विद्यालयः गच्छति → सः विद्यालयं गच्छति. 5) अनुस्वारत्रुटिः: सस्कृतम् → संस्कृतम्. (Also acceptable: विसर्गत्रुटिः दुखम् → दुःखम्; संयुक्ताक्षर/हलन्त/पदच्छेद errors विदया → विद्या, भगवान → भगवान्, सःपाठंपठति → सः पाठं पठति.)
questions.explanation: Any five families with a valid pair each earn full marks.

questions.question: Correct the matra errors: (a) परिक्षा (b) सुर्यः (c) नदि (d) जिवनम्.
questions.answer: (a) परीक्षा — परि + ईक्षा gives the long ई. (b) सूर्यः — long ऊ matra. (c) नदी — the feminine stem ends in long ई. (d) जीवनम् — जीव has long ई. All four are मात्रात्रुटयः (short vowel-sign printed for a long one).
questions.explanation: Each word needs its long vowel-sign restored.

questions.question: The printer has glued these words without sandhi. Fix each and name the rule: (a) सूर्यउदयः (b) इतिआदि.
questions.answer: (a) सूर्य + उदयः = सूर्योदयः — गुणसन्धिः (अ + उ = ओ). (b) इति + आदि = इत्यादि — यण्सन्धिः (the इ of इति becomes य् before the unlike vowel आ).
questions.explanation: Split, apply the vowel-sandhi rule, re-join.

questions.question: Correct the case/agreement errors and explain: (a) सः विद्यालयः गच्छति। (b) बालकाः पठति।
questions.answer: (a) सः विद्यालयं गच्छति। — the destination of motion stands in द्वितीया (accusative), so विद्यालयः must become विद्यालयम्/विद्यालयं. (b) बालकाः पठन्ति। — the subject is plural, so the verb must be plural: पठन्ति, not the singular पठति.
questions.explanation: Destination takes द्वितीया; verb agrees with subject in number.

questions.question: Proof-read this passage: 'रामः प्रतिदिनं विधालयं गच्छति। सः सस्कृतं पठति। तस्य परिक्षा शीघ्रं भविष्यति। सः उतमः छात्रः अस्ति।' Find all five errors (count विधालयं as one), write the corrected passage, and state the rule behind each fix.
questions.answer:
Corrected passage: रामः प्रतिदिनं विद्यालयं गच्छति। सः संस्कृतं पठति। तस्य परीक्षा शीघ्रं भविष्यति। सः उत्तमः छात्रः अस्ति।
Fixes: 1) विधालयं → विद्यालयं — conjunct error; the word is विद्या + आलयः, needing the conjunct द्य (and दीर्घसन्धिः आ + आ = आ). 2) सस्कृतं → संस्कृतं — अनुस्वारत्रुटिः; the nasal dot is part of the word संस्कृतम्. 3) परिक्षा → परीक्षा — मात्रात्रुटिः; परि + ईक्षा gives long ई. 4) उतमः → उत्तमः — conjunct error; the word has double त्त. 5) The passage as printed also demonstrates the method: reading word by word (शब्दशः पठनम्) is what exposes these four small slips that sense-reading would glide over.
questions.explanation: Four textual corrections with rules, plus method awareness.

questions.question: Describe the seven-step method of careful proof-reading (शोधनविधिः) taught in this lesson, explaining briefly why each step is needed.
questions.answer: 1) मूलपाठेन तुलना — compare the proof with the original line by line, because memory cannot be trusted. 2) शब्दशः पठनम् — read word by word, since the eye reading for sense silently auto-corrects errors. 3) मात्रा-बिन्दु-परीक्षा — inspect every matra, anusvāra dot, visarga and halant, because single strokes carry grammar. 4) व्याकरणपरीक्षा — test junctions by sandhi rules and endings by vibhakti roles; split doubtful sandhis and re-join. 5) उच्चैः पठनम् — read aloud once; the ear catches wrong vowels and broken rhythm the eye misses. 6) द्वितीयं पठनम् — give a second pass after a gap, or use a second reader; fresh eyes find what tired eyes forgive. 7) संशोधनचिह्नानि — mark each correction cleanly in the margin with standard proof-marks, never over the text.
questions.explanation: All seven steps with a one-line justification each.

questions.question: Correct the anusvāra/visarga errors and state the rule: (a) दुखम् (b) ससारः (c) पुन.
questions.answer: (a) दुःखम् — the visarga ः inside दुःखम् is a real sound; without it the word is meaningless. (b) संसारः — the anusvāra dot is part of the word (सं + सारः). (c) पुनः — the adverb 'again' ends in visarga; without it the word is incomplete.
questions.explanation: Two visarga restorations and one anusvāra restoration.

questions.question: Fix the conjunct errors: (a) विदया (b) प्रशनः. Name the conjunct that was broken in each.
questions.answer: (a) विद्या — the conjunct द्य (द् + य) was printed as two full letters दया. (b) प्रश्नः — the conjunct श्न (श् + न) was printed as शन. Both are संयुक्ताक्षरत्रुटयः (broken-conjunct errors).
questions.explanation: Restore द्य and श्न.

questions.question: Show with the pairs मासः/मांसः and दिनम्/दीनम् how a single printing slip can change the meaning of a Sanskrit word. What lesson does the proof-reader draw from such pairs?
questions.answer: मासः means 'a month', but adding one anusvāra dot makes मांसः, 'flesh' — a completely different word. दिनम् means 'a day', but lengthening one matra makes दीनम्, 'poor/wretched'. The lesson: in Sanskrit a single dot or stroke can replace one word with another, so the proof-reader must check every anusvāra, visarga and matra individually (मात्रा-बिन्दु-परीक्षा), and never assume a small slip is harmless.
questions.explanation: Meaning-changing minimal pairs motivate letter-level checking.

questions.question: 'मुद्रणम्' इत्यस्य पदस्य अर्थः कः? (What does मुद्रणम् mean?)
questions.explanation: मुद्रणम् means printing; मुद्रणत्रुटिः is therefore a printing error.

questions.question: 'शोधनम्' इत्यस्य अर्थः कः? (What does शोधनम् mean?)
questions.explanation: शोधनम् = correction, purification; here, the correcting of printing errors.

questions.question: मुद्रणत्रुटिशोधनम् is best translated as
questions.explanation: मुद्रणम् + त्रुटिः + शोधनम् = the correction of printing errors, i.e. proof-reading.

questions.question: Why is proof-reading especially critical in Sanskrit?
options: A single dot or matra can change the meaning of a word
Sanskrit is always written without vowel-signs
questions.answer: A single dot or matra can change the meaning of a word
questions.explanation: E.g. मासः (month) vs मांसः (flesh); दिनम् (day) vs दीनम् (wretched).

questions.question: The person who reads a printed proof and marks its errors is called
questions.explanation: संशोधकः = the proof-reader / corrector; his work is संशोधनम्.

questions.question: The lesson calls careful proof-reading 'अर्थरक्षणम्' because
options: correcting errors protects the meaning of the text
it earns money for the printer
it makes the page look beautiful
questions.answer: correcting errors protects the meaning of the text
questions.explanation: अर्थरक्षणम् = guarding of meaning; errors like मासः → मांसः destroy meaning.

questions.question: According to the lesson, the proof-reader's two essential tools are
options: a patient eye (सूक्ष्मदृष्टिः) and sound grammar (व्याकरणज्ञानम्)
a fast pen and a loud voice
questions.answer: a patient eye (सूक्ष्मदृष्टिः) and sound grammar (व्याकरणज्ञानम्)
questions.explanation: You can only correct an error if you notice it AND know the correct form.

questions.question: An error in which one consonant is printed in place of another (e.g. वालकः for बालकः) is called
questions.explanation: अक्षरत्रुटिः = wrong-letter error; ब/व, ण/न, श/ष/स are the classic confusions.

questions.question: An error in the vowel-sign — a short इ printed for a long ई, for example — is called
questions.explanation: मात्रा = vowel-sign; swapping short and long matras is a मात्रात्रुटिः.

questions.question: The faulty word परिक्षा (for परीक्षा) shows which error type?
questions.explanation: The short ि was printed for the long ी of परीक्षा — a vowel-sign error.

questions.question: The faulty word रामायनम् (for रामायणम्) shows which error type?
questions.explanation: न was printed for ण — a wrong-letter error, fixed by the णत्व rule.

questions.question: The faulty form सूर्यउदयः (for सूर्योदयः) shows which error type?
questions.explanation: The words were glued without applying गुणसन्धिः (अ + उ = ओ).

questions.question: The faulty sentence 'सः विद्यालयः गच्छति' shows which error type?
questions.explanation: The destination must be द्वितीया: सः विद्यालयं गच्छति — a case-ending error.

questions.question: The faulty word दुखम् (for दुःखम्) shows which error type?
questions.explanation: The visarga ः inside दुःखम् has been dropped — a visarga error.

questions.question: The faulty word विदया (for विद्या) shows which error type?
questions.explanation: The conjunct द्य was printed as the two full letters दया — a broken-conjunct error.

questions.question: The faulty string 'सःपाठंपठति' (for सः पाठं पठति) shows which error type?
questions.explanation: Three separate words have been glued into one string — a word-division error.

questions.question: The faulty word भगवान (for भगवान्) shows which error type?
questions.explanation: The word ends in the bare consonant न्, which needs the halant stroke: भगवान्.

questions.question: शुद्धं रूपं किम्? (Which form is correct?)
questions.explanation: परि + ईक्षा = परीक्षा with long ई — the others are matra/letter errors.

questions.question: शुद्धं रूपं किम्?
questions.explanation: सूर्यः needs the long ू matra; सुर्यः is a मात्रात्रुटिः.

questions.question: शुद्धं रूपं किम्?
questions.explanation: कीर्तिः (fame) has long ई and the conjunct र्त.

questions.question: शुद्धं रूपं किम्?
questions.explanation: The feminine noun नदी (river) ends in long ई.

questions.question: शुद्धं रूपं किम्?
questions.explanation: पूजा (worship) has the long ू matra.

questions.question: शुद्धं रूपं किम्?
questions.explanation: मूर्खः (fool) has long ऊ and the conjunct र्ख.

questions.question: The stem गुरु ends in a SHORT उ. Which nominative form is correctly printed?
questions.explanation: गुरुः has short उ; गुरूः is the opposite matra error (long for short).

questions.question: शुद्धं रूपं किम्?
questions.explanation: भूमिः (earth) has long ऊ in the first syllable and short इ in the second.

questions.question: शुद्धं रूपं किम्?
questions.explanation: जीवनम् (life) has the long ी matra.

questions.question: शुद्धं रूपं किम्?
questions.explanation: दीपः (lamp) has the long ी matra.

questions.question: By the णत्व rule, which is the correct form?
questions.explanation: न becomes ण after र् within the word: रामायणम्.

questions.question: By the णत्व rule, which is the correct form?
questions.explanation: After र्, the न of the suffix becomes ण: कारणम् (cause).

questions.question: By the षत्व rule, which is the correct form?
questions.explanation: The correct sibilant here is the retroflex ष: भाषा (language).

questions.question: शुद्धं रूपं किम्?
questions.explanation: पुरुषः (man) takes the retroflex ष by the षत्व rule.

questions.question: 'Boy' in Sanskrit is correctly printed as
questions.explanation: बालकः begins with ब; printing व (वालकः) is an अक्षरत्रुटिः.

questions.question: विद्या + आलयः = ? (correct sandhi)
questions.explanation: दीर्घसन्धिः: आ + आ = आ, giving विद्यालयः.

questions.question: सूर्य + उदयः = ? (correct sandhi)
questions.explanation: गुणसन्धिः: अ + उ = ओ, giving सूर्योदयः.

questions.question: देव + इन्द्रः = ? (correct sandhi)
questions.explanation: गुणसन्धिः: अ + इ = ए, giving देवेन्द्रः.

questions.question: गण + ईशः = ? (correct sandhi)
questions.explanation: गुणसन्धिः: अ + ई = ए, giving गणेशः.

questions.question: सदा + एव = ? (correct sandhi)
questions.explanation: वृद्धिसन्धिः: आ + ए = ऐ, giving सदैव.

questions.question: महा + ऋषिः = ? (correct sandhi)
questions.explanation: गुणसन्धिः: आ + ऋ = अर्, giving महर्षिः.

questions.question: इति + आदि = ? (correct sandhi)
questions.explanation: यण्सन्धिः: the इ of इति becomes य् before the unlike vowel आ.

questions.question: सु + आगतम् = ? (correct sandhi)
questions.explanation: यण्सन्धिः: उ becomes व् before the unlike vowel आ — स्वागतम् (welcome).

questions.question: मनः + रथः = ? (correct visarga sandhi)
questions.explanation: Before the soft (voiced) र्, the visarga of मनः becomes ओ: मनोरथः.

questions.question: निः + चयः = ? (correct visarga sandhi)
questions.explanation: Before च्, the visarga becomes श्: निश्चयः (certainty).

questions.question: नमः + ते = ? (correct visarga sandhi)
questions.explanation: Before त्, the visarga becomes स्: नमस्ते.

questions.question: सत् + जनः = ? (correct consonant sandhi)
questions.explanation: त् + ज् = ज्ज् : सज्जनः (a good man).

questions.question: जगत् + नाथः = ? (correct consonant sandhi)
questions.explanation: त् before न् becomes the nasal न्: जगन्नाथः.

questions.question: शुद्धं वाक्यं किम्? (Which sentence is correct?)
questions.explanation: The destination of motion stands in द्वितीया: विद्यालयम्/विद्यालयं.

questions.question: शुद्धं वाक्यं किम्?
questions.explanation: Subject in प्रथमा (बालकः), object in द्वितीया (दुग्धं).

questions.question: 'The student writes with a pen.' — शुद्धं वाक्यं किम्?
questions.explanation: The instrument stands in तृतीया: लेखन्या (with a pen).

questions.question: 'The boy falls from the tree.' — शुद्धं वाक्यं किम्?
questions.explanation: The point of separation ('from') stands in पञ्चमी: वृक्षात्.

questions.question: 'He gives clothing to the poor man.' — शुद्धं वाक्यं किम्?
questions.explanation: The recipient stands in चतुर्थी: निर्धनाय (to the poor man).

questions.question: 'Rama's book' is correctly printed as
questions.explanation: Possession stands in षष्ठी: रामस्य (of Rama).

questions.question: 'He lives in the city.' — शुद्धं वाक्यं किम्?
questions.explanation: Location stands in सप्तमी: नगरे (in the city).

questions.question: Which is the correct form of address (सम्बोधनम्)?
questions.explanation: The vocative singular of बालक is हे बालक (no visarga).

questions.question: शुद्धं वाक्यं किम्? (agreement)
questions.explanation: A plural subject needs the plural verb क्रीडन्ति.

questions.question: शुद्धं वाक्यं किम्? (person agreement)
questions.explanation: With अहम् (I), the verb takes the first-person ending: पठामि.

questions.question: शुद्धं वाक्यं किम्? (person agreement)
questions.explanation: With त्वम् (you), the verb takes the second-person ending: गच्छसि.

questions.question: शुद्धं वाक्यं किम्? (person and number agreement)
questions.explanation: With वयम् (we), the verb takes the first-person plural ending: गच्छामः.

questions.question: शुद्धं रूपं किम्?
questions.explanation: संस्कृतम् needs its anusvāra dot; सस्कृतम् is an अनुस्वारत्रुटिः.

questions.question: शुद्धं रूपं किम्?
questions.explanation: संसारः (the world) carries the anusvāra: सं + सारः.

questions.question: शुद्धं रूपं किम्?
questions.explanation: The nasal conjunct न्द must not be flattened: सुन्दरम् (beautiful).

questions.question: The river 'Ganga' is correctly printed as
questions.explanation: गङ्गा has the nasal conjunct ङ्ग; गगा drops the nasal entirely.

questions.question: शुद्धं रूपं किम्?
questions.explanation: दुःखम् (sorrow) has the visarga ः inside the word.

questions.question: शुद्धं रूपं किम्?
questions.explanation: अन्तः + करणम् keeps the internal visarga, and णत्व gives करणम् with ण.

questions.question: The word for 'again' is correctly printed as
questions.explanation: पुनः ends in visarga; dropping it (पुन) is a विसर्गत्रुटिः.

questions.question: 'Morning time' is correctly printed as
questions.explanation: प्रातः keeps its visarga inside the compound: प्रातःकालः.

questions.question: शुद्धं रूपं किम्?
questions.explanation: प्रश्नः (question) has the conjunct श्न.

questions.question: शुद्धं रूपं किम्?
questions.explanation: उत्तमः (best) has the double conjunct त्त.

questions.question: 'A learned man' is correctly printed as
questions.explanation: विद्वान् needs both the conjunct द्व and the final halant न्.

questions.question: A printer adds a stray anusvāra and मासः becomes मांसः. What has happened to the meaning?
options: 'Month' has become 'flesh' — a completely different word
The word has merely become plural
The word has become a verb
questions.answer: 'Month' has become 'flesh' — a completely different word
questions.explanation: मासः = month; मांसः = flesh. One dot replaces the word itself.

questions.question: Why must a proof-reader read शब्दशः (word by word) rather than by the flow of sense?
options: The eye reading for sense silently auto-corrects errors and slides past them
Sanskrit cannot be read by sense
questions.answer: The eye reading for sense silently auto-corrects errors and slides past them
questions.explanation: The proof-reader must read what is actually printed, not what ought to be printed.

questions.question: What is the purpose of उच्चैः पठनम् (reading aloud) in proof-reading?
options: The ear catches wrong vowels and broken rhythm that the eye misses
It replaces the need for grammar
questions.answer: The ear catches wrong vowels and broken rhythm that the eye misses
questions.explanation: Aloud reading is step 5 of the शोधनविधिः.

questions.question: According to the method, where should corrections be marked on a proof?
options: Clearly in the margin, with standard proof-marks
On a separate book, from memory
questions.answer: Clearly in the margin, with standard proof-marks
questions.explanation: संशोधनचिह्नानि go in the margin; never scribble over the text.

questions.question: Why does the method demand a द्वितीयं पठनम् (second pass or second reader)?
options: Fresh eyes find what tired eyes forgive
The first reading is never done carefully
questions.answer: Fresh eyes find what tired eyes forgive
questions.explanation: A gap, or another reader, catches the errors the first pass missed.

questions.question: In the printed sentence 'रामं वनं गच्छति।' the error is that
options: the subject must be रामः (प्रथमा), not रामं
questions.answer: the subject must be रामः (प्रथमा), not रामं
questions.explanation: The doer stands in प्रथमा: रामः वनं गच्छति।

questions.question: Proof-read: 'बालिका सुन्दरः अस्ति।' Which correction is right?
options: सुन्दरः → सुन्दरी (the adjective must be feminine)
questions.answer: सुन्दरः → सुन्दरी (the adjective must be feminine)
questions.explanation: The adjective agrees with the feminine noun बालिका: सुन्दरी बालिका.

questions.question: True or False: मात्रात्रुटिः means an error in the vowel-sign, such as printing नदि for नदी.
questions.explanation: मात्रा = vowel-sign; swapping short and long matras is a मात्रात्रुटिः.

questions.question: True or False: An anusvāra error can change the meaning of a word — मासः (month) with a stray dot becomes मांसः (flesh).
questions.explanation: One dot can replace a word with a different word entirely.

questions.question: True or False: परिक्षा is the correctly printed form of the word for 'examination'.
questions.explanation: The correct form is परीक्षा, with long ई (परि + ईक्षा).

questions.question: True or False: सूर्य + उदयः joins as सूर्योदयः by the गुण sandhi rule (अ + उ = ओ).
questions.explanation: गुणसन्धिः gives ओ at the junction: सूर्योदयः.

questions.question: True or False: In 'सः ग्रामं गच्छति', the destination ग्रामं correctly stands in the द्वितीया (accusative) case.
questions.explanation: The destination of motion takes द्वितीया.

questions.question: True or False: A proof should be read fast and by the flow of sense, because that is how errors are best caught.
questions.explanation: The opposite: read slowly, word by word — sense-reading auto-corrects and hides errors.

questions.question: True or False: नमः + ते correctly joins as नमःते.
questions.explanation: Before त्, the visarga becomes स्: नमस्ते.

questions.question: True or False: Printing दुखम् for दुःखम् is a विसर्गत्रुटिः (visarga error).
questions.explanation: The internal visarga of दुःखम् has been dropped.

questions.question: True or False: A printing error never changes the meaning of a Sanskrit word; it only affects the appearance of the page.
questions.explanation: Errors like दिनम् → दीनम् and मासः → मांसः change the meaning completely.

questions.question: True or False: सत् + जनः correctly joins as सज्जनः (त् + ज् = ज्ज्).
questions.explanation: The dental त् assimilates to the following ज्: सज्जनः.

questions.question: Correct the printed word: परिक्षा → ____ (examination)
questions.explanation: मात्रात्रुटिः: परि + ईक्षा needs the long ी.

questions.question: Correct the printed word: सुर्यः → ____ (the sun)
questions.explanation: The long ू matra was printed short.

questions.question: Correct the printed word: नदि → ____ (river)
questions.explanation: The feminine noun नदी ends in long ई.

questions.question: Correct the printed word: जिवनम् → ____ (life)
questions.explanation: जीव has the long ी matra.

questions.question: Correct the printed word by the णत्व rule: रामायनम् → ____
questions.explanation: न becomes ण after र् within the word.

questions.question: Correct the printed word by the षत्व rule: भासा → ____ (language)
questions.explanation: The correct sibilant is the retroflex ष.

questions.question: Join with the correct sandhi: सूर्य + उदयः = ____
questions.explanation: गुणसन्धिः: अ + उ = ओ.

questions.question: Join with the correct sandhi: इति + आदि = ____
questions.explanation: यण्सन्धिः: इ becomes य् before आ.

questions.question: Join with the correct visarga sandhi: मनः + रथः = ____
questions.explanation: Visarga becomes ओ before the voiced र्.

questions.question: Correct the printed word: दुखम् → ____ (sorrow)
questions.explanation: The internal visarga ः must be restored.

questions.question: Correct the printed word: ससारः → ____ (the world)
questions.explanation: The anusvāra dot must be restored: सं + सारः.

questions.question: Correct the printed word: विदया → ____ (knowledge)
questions.explanation: The conjunct द्य must be restored.

questions.question: Correct the printed word: प्रशनः → ____ (question)
questions.explanation: The conjunct श्न must be restored.

questions.question: Correct the verb (plural agreement): बालकाः ____ । (पठ्, to read)
questions.explanation: A plural subject takes the plural verb पठन्ति.

questions.question: Supply the correct case-form: सः ____ गच्छति। (विद्यालय — as the destination)
questions.explanation: The destination of motion stands in द्वितीया: विद्यालयम्/विद्यालयं.

questions.question: Define मुद्रणत्रुटिः and give one example of such an error together with its correction.
questions.answer: A मुद्रणत्रुटिः is a printing error — any slip of letter, matra, dot, sandhi, case-ending or word-division that enters a text during typing or printing. Example: परिक्षा printed for परीक्षा (a matra error); the proof-reader corrects the short ि to the long ी.
questions.explanation: Definition plus any valid wrong → correct pair.

questions.question: Why does the lesson say that in Sanskrit proof-reading 'every dot matters'? Give two examples.
questions.answer: Because single dots and strokes carry grammar and meaning. (1) The anusvāra: मासः (month) with a stray dot becomes मांसः (flesh) — a different word. (2) The visarga: दुःखम् without its ः becomes the meaningless दुखम्, and बालकः without ः loses its subject-marker. Hence every anusvāra and visarga must be checked individually.
questions.explanation: Anusvāra and visarga both carry meaning and grammar.

questions.question: List the seven families of printing errors taught in this chapter.
questions.answer: 1) अक्षरत्रुटिः (wrong letter), 2) मात्रात्रुटिः (wrong vowel-sign), 3) सन्धित्रुटिः (wrong/omitted sandhi), 4) विभक्तित्रुटिः (wrong case-ending or agreement), 5) अनुस्वारत्रुटिः (missing/stray anusvāra), 6) विसर्गत्रुटिः (missing/stray visarga), 7) संयुक्ताक्षर-हलन्त-पदच्छेदत्रुटयः (broken conjuncts, missing halants, wrong word-division).
questions.explanation: The full taxonomy of the chapter.

questions.question: Distinguish between अक्षरत्रुटिः and मात्रात्रुटिः, with one example of each.
questions.answer: An अक्षरत्रुटिः prints one consonant for another — e.g. वालकः for बालकः (व for ब). A मात्रात्रुटिः prints the wrong vowel-sign — e.g. नदि for नदी (short ि for long ी). The first error is in the letter itself; the second is in the vowel-mark attached to it.
questions.explanation: Consonant error vs vowel-sign error.

questions.question: Correct these words and name the error: (a) किर्तिः (b) मुर्खः.
questions.answer: (a) कीर्तिः — the long ई matra was printed short; a मात्रात्रुटिः. (b) मूर्खः — the long ऊ matra was printed short; also a मात्रात्रुटिः.
questions.explanation: Both are short-for-long vowel-sign errors.

questions.question: Correct these words and state the rule: (a) कारनम् (b) प्रनामः.
questions.answer: (a) कारणम् (b) प्रणामः. Rule: णत्वम् — within a word, न becomes the retroflex ण after र् (the र of कार- and प्र- triggers the change). Both printed forms are अक्षरत्रुटयः.
questions.explanation: The णत्व rule converts न to ण after र्.

questions.question: Give two minimal pairs in which a single matra or dot changes the meaning of a Sanskrit word, and explain why such errors are the most dangerous for a proof-reader.
questions.answer: Pairs: दिनम् (day) / दीनम् (poor, wretched) — one matra; मासः (month) / मांसः (flesh) — one anusvāra dot; also सुतः (son) / सूतः (charioteer). These are the most dangerous because the faulty form is itself a real word: the sentence still 'reads', no alarm is raised, and only careful letter-by-letter checking against the original will catch the substitution.
questions.explanation: Real-word substitutions escape casual reading.

questions.question: Do the सन्धिविच्छेद (split) and name the rule: (a) विद्यालयः (b) सदैव.
questions.answer: (a) विद्यालयः = विद्या + आलयः — दीर्घसन्धिः (आ + आ = आ). (b) सदैव = सदा + एव — वृद्धिसन्धिः (आ + ए = ऐ).
questions.explanation: Splitting confirms which joining rule was applied.

questions.question: Join correctly and name the rule: (a) देव + इन्द्रः (b) महा + ऋषिः.
questions.answer: (a) देवेन्द्रः — गुणसन्धिः (अ + इ = ए). (b) महर्षिः — गुणसन्धिः (आ + ऋ = अर्).
questions.explanation: Both junctions follow the guna rule.

questions.question: The printer left these unsandhied. Fix both and name the rule: (a) सुआगतम् (b) प्रतिएकम्.
questions.answer: (a) स्वागतम् — यण्सन्धिः: the उ of सु becomes व् before the unlike vowel आ. (b) प्रत्येकम् — यण्सन्धिः: the इ of प्रति becomes य् before ए.
questions.explanation: यण् turns इ/उ into य्/व् before unlike vowels.

questions.question: Correct these visarga-sandhi errors and state each rule: (a) निःचयः (b) नमःते (c) पुनःअपि.
questions.answer: (a) निश्चयः — before च्, the visarga becomes श्. (b) नमस्ते — before त्, the visarga becomes स्. (c) पुनरपि — the visarga of पुनः becomes र् before a vowel: पुनर् + अपि.
questions.explanation: Visarga assimilates to the following sound.

questions.question: Correct and explain: 'सः विद्यालयः गच्छति।'
questions.answer: Corrected: सः विद्यालयं गच्छति। The place one goes TO (the destination of motion) stands in द्वितीया (accusative). The printed विद्यालयः wrongly keeps the nominative, as if the school itself were the subject.
questions.explanation: Destination takes द्वितीया.

questions.question: Correct and explain: 'छात्रः लेखनी लिखति।' (The student writes with a pen.)
questions.answer: Corrected: छात्रः लेखन्या लिखति। The pen is the instrument of the action, and the instrument stands in तृतीया (instrumental): लेखन्या = 'with the pen'. The nominative लेखनी would absurdly make the pen a second subject.
questions.explanation: The instrument takes तृतीया.

questions.question: Correct and explain: 'बालकः वृक्षस्य पतति।' (The boy falls from the tree.)
questions.answer: Corrected: बालकः वृक्षात् पतति। The point from which separation or falling happens stands in पञ्चमी (ablative): वृक्षात् = 'from the tree'. The genitive वृक्षस्य ('of the tree') does not express 'from'.
questions.explanation: अपादान (source of separation) takes पञ्चमी.

questions.question: Fix the agreement errors and explain: (a) ते गच्छति। (b) अहं पठति। (c) त्वं पठति।
questions.answer: (a) ते गच्छन्ति। — plural subject, plural verb. (b) अहं पठामि। — first-person subject takes the first-person ending -आमि. (c) त्वं पठसि। — second-person subject takes the ending -सि. A Sanskrit verb must agree with its subject in both person and number.
questions.explanation: Verb agrees with subject in person and number.

questions.question: Explain the difference between मासः and मांसः. Which single sign separates them?
questions.answer: मासः means 'a month'; मांसः means 'flesh/meat'. They are separated by a single anusvāra dot (ं) on the first syllable. This shows why the proof-reader must verify every dot: adding or dropping one anusvāra swaps one real word for another.
questions.explanation: A one-dot minimal pair.

questions.question: Correct the visarga errors: (a) अन्तकरणम् (b) प्रातकालः (c) बालक क्रीडति।
questions.answer: (a) अन्तःकरणम् — the compound अन्तः + करणम् keeps its internal visarga. (b) प्रातःकालः — प्रातः keeps its visarga inside the compound. (c) बालकः क्रीडति। — the subject needs its nominative visarga; without it the word is left caseless.
questions.explanation: Internal and final visargas must be restored.

questions.question: Correct the conjunct errors: (a) अधययनम् (b) विदवान् (c) धरमः. Name the conjunct restored in each.
questions.answer: (a) अध्ययनम् — the conjunct ध्य (ध् + य). (b) विद्वान् — the conjunct द्व (द् + व). (c) धर्मः — the conjunct र्म (र् above म, the repha). All three printed forms flattened a conjunct into two full letters.
questions.explanation: Broken conjuncts are restored: ध्य, द्व, र्म.

questions.question: Why do भगवान and हनुमान need correction at their final letter? Write the correct forms.
questions.answer: Both words end in the bare consonant न्, which must carry the halant stroke: भगवान्, हनुमान्. Printed without the halant (भगवान, हनुमान) they wrongly end in the full syllable न (na). This is a हलन्तत्रुटिः.
questions.explanation: Consonant-ending words need the halant stroke.

questions.question: List, in order, the seven steps of the शोधनविधिः (proof-reading method).
questions.answer: 1) मूलपाठेन तुलना — compare with the original line by line. 2) शब्दशः पठनम् — read word by word. 3) मात्रा-बिन्दु-परीक्षा — check every matra, anusvāra, visarga and halant. 4) व्याकरणपरीक्षा — test sandhis and case-endings by rule. 5) उच्चैः पठनम् — read aloud. 6) द्वितीयं पठनम् — second pass or second reader. 7) संशोधनचिह्नानि — mark corrections in the margin with standard signs.
questions.explanation: The seven steps in sequence.

questions.question: Why does the method insist on both उच्चैः पठनम् (reading aloud) and द्वितीयं पठनम् (a second pass)?
questions.answer: Reading aloud engages the ear, which catches wrong vowels, missing sounds and broken rhythm that the eye glides over. A second pass — after a gap, or by another reader — works because fresh eyes find what tired eyes forgive; the first reading always leaves some errors undetected.
questions.explanation: Ear-checking plus fresh-eyes checking.

questions.question: Fix the word-division (पदच्छेद) errors: (a) 'सःपाठंपठति' (b) 'विद्या लयः'.
questions.answer: (a) सः पाठं पठति — three words were glued into one string; they must be separated. (b) विद्यालयः — one word was wrongly split into two; विद्या + आलयः join by दीर्घसन्धिः into the single word विद्यालयः.
questions.explanation: Gluing and splitting are both पदच्छेद errors.

questions.question: Explain the nature and importance of मुद्रणत्रुटिशोधनम्. Why is it called अर्थरक्षणम्, what qualities does a संशोधकः need, and what can happen if proofs are not read carefully?
questions.answer: मुद्रणत्रुटिशोधनम् (मुद्रणम् + त्रुटिः + शोधनम्) is the systematic correction of printing errors — proof-reading. Sanskrit packs grammar into single sounds: the visarga of रामः marks the subject, the anusvāra of रामं marks the object, the halant of भगवान् marks a consonant-ending word. A dropped dot therefore changes the grammar of the sentence, and some slips replace a word with a different real word: मासः (month) becomes मांसः (flesh), दिनम् (day) becomes दीनम् (wretched). Because correcting errors literally protects the meaning of the text, the work is called अर्थरक्षणम् — the guarding of meaning. The संशोधकः needs two qualities: सूक्ष्मदृष्टिः, a sharp and patient eye that inspects every matra and dot, and व्याकरणज्ञानम्, sound grammar, since one can only correct an error if one knows the correct form. If proofs are not read carefully, corrupted texts spread: students memorise wrong forms, meanings shift, and the authority of the printed book passes the error on to every reader.
questions.explanation: Definition, meaning-changing examples, the proof-reader's qualities, and consequences.

questions.question: Describe the seven families of printing errors taught in this chapter, giving one wrong → correct example for each family.
questions.answer: 1) अक्षरत्रुटिः — wrong letter: वालकः → बालकः; रामायनम् → रामायणम् (णत्व); भासा → भाषा (षत्व). 2) मात्रात्रुटिः — wrong vowel-sign: परिक्षा → परीक्षा; नदि → नदी; गुरूः → गुरुः. 3) सन्धित्रुटिः — wrong or omitted junction: सूर्यउदयः → सूर्योदयः (गुण); इतिआदि → इत्यादि (यण्). 4) विभक्तित्रुटिः — wrong case or agreement: सः विद्यालयः गच्छति → सः विद्यालयं गच्छति; बालकाः पठति → बालकाः पठन्ति. 5) अनुस्वारत्रुटिः — missing or stray dot: सस्कृतम् → संस्कृतम्; and the meaning-change मासः/मांसः. 6) विसर्गत्रुटिः — missing or stray visarga: दुखम् → दुःखम्; पुन → पुनः. 7) संयुक्ताक्षर-हलन्त-पदच्छेदत्रुटयः — broken conjuncts (विदया → विद्या, प्रशनः → प्रश्नः), missing halants (भगवान → भगवान्), and wrong word-division (सःपाठंपठति → सः पाठं पठति).
questions.explanation: Full taxonomy with a valid pair for each family.

questions.question: Explain the णत्व and षत्व rules that the proof-reader uses against letter errors, and correct these five words: रामायनम्, कारनम्, परिनामः, भासा, पुरुशः.
questions.answer: णत्व rule: within a word, the dental न becomes the retroflex ण when it follows र् (even at a distance, unless certain letters intervene). Hence रामायनम् → रामायणम्, कारनम् → कारणम्, परिनामः → परिणामः — in each, a र earlier in the word triggers ण. षत्व rule: the स of many suffixes and stems becomes the retroflex ष after vowels other than अ/आ (इ, उ, ए etc.) and after र्. Hence भासा → भाषा and पुरुशः → पुरुषः (here the printed श was also the wrong sibilant — the rule demands ष). The proof-reader applies these two rules whenever he sees न/ण or श/ष/स hesitation: he asks 'is there a र् or a triggering vowel before this sound?' and restores the correct letter accordingly.
questions.explanation: Both retroflexion rules plus five corrections.

questions.question: Write a proof-reader's refresher of the main sandhi rules — दीर्घ, गुण, वृद्धि, यण् and विसर्ग sandhi — correcting one faulty printed form under each rule.
questions.answer: 1) दीर्घसन्धिः: like simple vowels merge into the long vowel (अ/आ + अ/आ = आ). Fix: विद्याआलयः → विद्यालयः (विद्या + आलयः). 2) गुणसन्धिः: अ/आ + इ/ई = ए; + उ/ऊ = ओ; + ऋ = अर्. Fix: सूर्यउदयः → सूर्योदयः; also देवेन्द्रः, महर्षिः. 3) वृद्धिसन्धिः: अ/आ + ए/ऐ = ऐ; + ओ/औ = औ. Fix: सदाएव → सदैव; also महौषधम्. 4) यण्सन्धिः: इ/ई, उ/ऊ become य्, व् before an unlike vowel. Fix: इतिआदि → इत्यादि; सुआगतम् → स्वागतम्. 5) विसर्गसन्धिः: the visarga becomes ओ before voiced sounds (मनःरथः → मनोरथः), श्/स् before the matching hard sounds (निःचयः → निश्चयः, नमःते → नमस्ते), and र् before vowels in forms like पुनःअपि → पुनरपि. Method: whenever a junction looks doubtful, split it (सन्धिविच्छेदः), identify the two meeting sounds, apply the rule afresh, and re-join.
questions.explanation: Five rule-families, each with a wrong → correct repair.

questions.question: Write a proof-reader's refresher of the seven vibhakti roles (with the singular forms of राम), and correct these printed sentences: (a) रामं वनं गच्छति। (b) छात्रः लेखनी लिखति। (c) बालकः वृक्षस्य पतति। (d) बालकाः पठति।
questions.answer: Roles with राम: प्रथमा रामः — subject; द्वितीया रामम् — object/destination; तृतीया रामेण — instrument (by/with); चतुर्थी रामाय — recipient (to/for); पञ्चमी रामात् — source (from); षष्ठी रामस्य — possession (of); सप्तमी रामे — location (in/at); सम्बोधनम् हे राम — address. The proof-reader asks of every noun: what role does it play, and does its ending match? Corrections: (a) रामः वनं गच्छति। — the doer must be प्रथमा. (b) छात्रः लेखन्या लिखति। — the pen is the instrument, so तृतीया. (c) बालकः वृक्षात् पतति। — falling FROM the tree is पञ्चमी. (d) बालकाः पठन्ति। — a plural subject demands the plural verb; verbs must agree with their subject in person and number, and adjectives with their noun in gender (सुन्दरी बालिका).
questions.explanation: Case roles plus four corrected sentences.

questions.question: Explain the anusvāra and visarga rules a proof-reader must know, with at least six corrected examples, and show with minimal pairs why these two signs deserve special attention.
questions.answer: Anusvāra rules: a word-final म् before a consonant is written as the dot ं (अहं गच्छामि); before a vowel it remains म् and joins (धनम् + आप्नोति = धनमाप्नोति). Nasal sounds inside words must not be dropped or flattened. Corrections: सस्कृतम् → संस्कृतम्; ससारः → संसारः; सुदरम् → सुन्दरम् (nasal conjunct न्द); गगा → गङ्गा (ङ्ग). Visarga rules: the visarga ः is a real sound, word-finally (रामः, पुनः) and word-internally (दुःखम्, अन्तःकरणम्); in sandhi it becomes ओ/श्/स्/र् by context (मनोरथः, निश्चयः, नमस्ते, पुनरपि). Corrections: दुखम् → दुःखम्; पुन → पुनः; प्रातकालः → प्रातःकालः; बालक क्रीडति → बालकः क्रीडति. Minimal pairs show the stakes: मासः (month) vs मांसः (flesh) differ by one anusvāra — both are real words, so the error hides in plain sight; and a dropped visarga strips the subject-marker from रामः. Hence the method's third step is exactly मात्रा-बिन्दु-परीक्षा: check every dot and stroke one by one.
questions.explanation: Rules, six-plus repairs, and the minimal-pair argument.

questions.question: Describe in detail the seven-step शोधनविधिः (method of careful proof-reading), justifying each step, and explain which kinds of errors each step is best at catching.
questions.answer: 1) मूलपाठेन तुलना — compare the proof with the original line by line; catches omissions, insertions and word-division errors, since memory cannot be trusted. 2) शब्दशः पठनम् — read word by word, not by sense; the sense-reading eye auto-corrects, so this step exposes letter and matra errors (परिक्षा, वालकः). 3) मात्रा-बिन्दु-परीक्षा — inspect every matra, anusvāra, visarga and halant; catches the one-dot errors (संस्कृतम्, दुःखम्, भगवान्). 4) व्याकरणपरीक्षा — test every junction by sandhi rules (split and re-join: सूर्योदयः) and every noun-ending by vibhakti roles (सः विद्यालयं गच्छति); catches sandhi and case errors. 5) उच्चैः पठनम् — read aloud once; the ear hears wrong vowels and broken rhythm the eye misses. 6) द्वितीयं पठनम् — a second pass after a gap, or a second reader; fresh eyes find what tired eyes forgive, so residual errors surface. 7) संशोधनचिह्नानि — write each correction in the margin with standard proof-marks, never over the text, so the compositor can apply every fix unambiguously.
questions.explanation: Seven steps, each justified and matched to error kinds.

questions.question:
Proof-read this printed passage, write the fully corrected version, and justify every correction with its rule:
'सूर्यउदयः अतीव सुदरः भवति। बालकाः नदि-तीरे क्रीडति। ते दुखम् न जानन्ति।'
questions.answer:
Corrected passage: सूर्योदयः अतीव सुन्दरः भवति। बालकाः नदी-तीरे क्रीडन्ति। ते दुःखं न जानन्ति।
Justifications: 1) सूर्यउदयः → सूर्योदयः — सन्धित्रुटिः; गुणसन्धिः joins सूर्य + उदयः with अ + उ = ओ. 2) सुदरः → सुन्दरः — अनुस्वार/nasal error; the nasal conjunct न्द of सुन्दर must not be flattened. 3) नदि → नदी — मात्रात्रुटिः; the feminine noun नदी ends in long ई. 4) क्रीडति → क्रीडन्ति — विभक्ति/agreement error; the plural subject बालकाः requires the plural verb. 5) दुखम् → दुःखं — विसर्गत्रुटिः; the internal visarga of दुःख must be restored, and the final म् is written as anusvāra before the following consonant न. The passage shows how one short text can carry errors from four different families, which is why the proof-reader works through the checklist rather than trusting a single glance.
questions.explanation: Five fixes across sandhi, nasal, matra, agreement and visarga.

questions.question:
A proof-reader receives this line: 'रामः प्रतिदिनं विधालयं गच्छति। तस्य परिक्षा शीघ्रं भविष्यति।'
(a) Find the two faulty words. (b) Correct each. (c) Name the error type of each. (d) State the rule behind each correction.
questions.answer: (a) The faulty words are विधालयं and परिक्षा. (b) Corrections: विद्यालयं and परीक्षा. (c) विधालयं is a संयुक्ताक्षरत्रुटिः (broken conjunct); परिक्षा is a मात्रात्रुटिः (short matra for long). (d) Rules: विद्यालयः = विद्या + आलयः — the conjunct द्य belongs to विद्या, and दीर्घसन्धिः (आ + आ = आ) joins the words; परीक्षा = परि + ईक्षा — the long ई must be written with the ी matra.
questions.explanation: Conjunct and matra repair with rules.

questions.question:
A typesetter has glued words without sandhi in this line: 'सूर्यउदये सः देवइन्द्रं स्मरति, इतिआदि वचनं पठति च।'
(a) Identify the three unsandhied forms. (b) Correct each. (c) Name the sandhi rule used in each correction.
questions.answer: (a) The unsandhied forms are सूर्यउदये, देवइन्द्रं and इतिआदि. (b) Corrections: सूर्योदये, देवेन्द्रं, इत्यादि. (c) Rules: सूर्य + उदये — गुणसन्धिः (अ + उ = ओ); देव + इन्द्रं — गुणसन्धिः (अ + इ = ए); इति + आदि — यण्सन्धिः (the इ of इति becomes य् before आ).
questions.explanation: Two guna junctions and one yan junction.

questions.question:
Proof-read this printed paragraph for case and agreement: 'बालकः दुग्धः पिबति। ततः सः विद्यालयः गच्छति। तत्र बालकाः पठति।'
(a) Find the three errors. (b) Correct each. (c) For each, state the case-role or agreement rule that was violated.
questions.answer: (a) The errors are दुग्धः, विद्यालयः and पठति. (b) Corrected paragraph: बालकः दुग्धं पिबति। ततः सः विद्यालयं गच्छति। तत्र बालकाः पठन्ति। (c) Rules: दुग्धं — the object of drinking stands in द्वितीया, not प्रथमा; विद्यालयं — the destination of motion stands in द्वितीया; पठन्ति — the plural subject बालकाः requires a plural verb (agreement in number).
questions.explanation: Object case, destination case, and verb-number agreement.

questions.question:
A proof contains this sentence: 'सः सस्कृतं पठित्वा ससारस्य दुखम् त्यजति।'
(a) Find the three words with anusvāra/visarga errors. (b) Correct each. (c) Say which sign (anusvāra or visarga) was dropped in each.
questions.answer: (a) The faulty words are सस्कृतं, ससारस्य and दुखम्. (b) Corrections: संस्कृतं, संसारस्य, दुःखम् — i.e. सः संस्कृतं पठित्वा संसारस्य दुःखं त्यजति। (c) In सस्कृतं and ससारस्य the anusvāra dot (ं) of सं- was dropped; in दुखम् the internal visarga (ः) of दुःख was dropped. (The final म् of दुःखम् may also be written as ं before the following consonant त्: दुःखं त्यजति.)
questions.explanation: Two anusvāra restorations and one visarga restoration.

questions.question:
Proof-read this whole printed passage: 'गुरूः शिष्यान् उपदिशति — विदया विनयं ददाति। सत्यं वद, धरमं चर। प्रशनः पृच्छ, उतमः भव।'
(a) Find the five faulty words. (b) Write the corrected passage. (c) Name each error type.
questions.answer: (a) The faulty words are गुरूः, विदया, धरमं, प्रशनः, उतमः. (b) Corrected: गुरुः शिष्यान् उपदिशति — विद्या विनयं ददाति। सत्यं वद, धर्मं चर। प्रश्नान् पृच्छ, उत्तमः भव। (c) गुरूः → गुरुः — मात्रात्रुटिः (the stem गुरु has short उ); विदया → विद्या — broken conjunct द्य; धरमं → धर्मं — broken conjunct र्म; प्रशनः → प्रश्नः/प्रश्नान् — broken conjunct श्न (and as the object of पृच्छ it should stand in द्वितीया: प्रश्नान्); उतमः → उत्तमः — broken conjunct त्त.
questions.explanation: One matra error and four conjunct errors, plus a case refinement.

questions.question:
A trainee proof-reader lists these faulty words from a proof: (1) वालकः (2) नदि (3) सूर्यउदयः (4) दुखम्।
Classify each into its error family, correct it, and state in one line how you recognised the family.
questions.answer: (1) वालकः — अक्षरत्रुटिः; correct बालकः; recognised because a wrong consonant (व for ब) was printed. (2) नदि — मात्रात्रुटिः; correct नदी; recognised because only the vowel-sign (short for long) is wrong. (3) सूर्यउदयः — सन्धित्रुटिः; correct सूर्योदयः; recognised because two words meet at a junction where no rule was applied (अ + उ should give ओ). (4) दुखम् — विसर्गत्रुटिः; correct दुःखम्; recognised because the visarga sign ः is missing from inside the word.
questions.explanation: Classification practice across four families.

questions.question:
A student proof-reads a chapter quickly, reading silently for sense, in a single pass, and marks corrections by overwriting the printed words. He misses many errors.
(a) Point out three faults in his procedure. (b) State which steps of the शोधनविधिः he should adopt instead, and why.
questions.answer: (a) Faults: (i) he reads for sense, so his eye auto-corrects and slides past errors; (ii) he gives only one pass, so residual errors are never caught; (iii) he overwrites the text, making his corrections ambiguous for the compositor. (b) He should: read शब्दशः (word by word), checking every matra and dot (मात्रा-बिन्दु-परीक्षा), because errors live in single strokes; read aloud once (उच्चैः पठनम्) so the ear catches what the eye misses; give a द्वितीयं पठनम् — a second pass after a gap or by a second reader — because fresh eyes find what tired eyes forgive; and mark corrections in the margin with standard संशोधनचिह्नानि so every fix is clear.
questions.explanation: Diagnosing bad procedure against the seven-step method.

questions.question:
A cookbook proof prints 'मासभोजनं वर्जयेत्' where the author wrote 'मांसभोजनं वर्जयेत्' (one should avoid meat-eating).
(a) What single sign was dropped? (b) How does the printed sentence's meaning differ from the author's? (c) What does this case teach about the importance of proof-reading?
questions.answer: (a) The anusvāra dot (ं) of मांस was dropped, turning मांस (flesh/meat) into मास (month). (b) The author's sentence means 'one should avoid meat-eating'; the printed sentence would suggest avoiding 'month-eating/eating for a month' — nonsense that could even be misread as advising a month-long fast. (c) It teaches that a single dot can invert or destroy an instruction: proof-reading is अर्थरक्षणम्, the guarding of meaning, and every anusvāra and visarga must be individually verified against the original (मात्रा-बिन्दु-परीक्षा), because the most dangerous errors produce real words that read smoothly.
questions.explanation: A one-dot error with real-world consequences.

questions.question:
This line of a devotional text is printed as: 'भगवान कृपालुः अस्ति। सः भक्तानां दुखानि हरति। वयं तं प्रणमामः।'
(a) Find the two faulty words. (b) Correct them. (c) Explain the halant rule and the visarga rule involved.
questions.answer: (a) The faulty words are भगवान and दुखानि. (b) Corrected: भगवान् कृपालुः अस्ति। सः भक्तानां दुःखानि हरति। वयं तं प्रणमामः। (c) Halant rule: भगवान् ends in the bare consonant न्, so it must carry the halant stroke; without it the word wrongly ends in the full syllable न. Visarga rule: the word दुःख has an internal visarga ः which is part of its very spelling; the plural दुःखानि keeps it. (Note प्रणमामः is correct as printed — the ण after प्र-र् follows the णत्व rule.)
questions.explanation: Halant restoration and internal-visarga restoration.

questions.question:
Final proof-reading test. The printed passage reads: 'अहं प्रातकालः उत्थाय नमःते इति वदामि। ततः अहं पुस्तकं पठति। मम माता सुन्दरः अस्ति।'
(a) Find the four errors. (b) Write the fully corrected passage. (c) Justify each correction with its rule.
questions.answer: (a) The errors are प्रातकालः, नमःते, पठति (after अहं) and सुन्दरः (with माता). (b) Corrected: अहं प्रातःकाले उत्थाय नमस्ते इति वदामि। ततः अहं पुस्तकं पठामि। मम माता सुन्दरी अस्ति। (c) Rules: प्रातःकाले — the visarga of प्रातः must be restored, and 'at morning time' stands in सप्तमी (locative); नमस्ते — विसर्गसन्धिः turns the visarga into स् before त् (नमः + ते); पठामि — the first-person subject अहम् demands the first-person verb-ending; सुन्दरी — the adjective must agree in gender with the feminine noun माता.
questions.explanation: Visarga, visarga-sandhi, person agreement and gender agreement.
